OpenAI just made its boldest move yet — into hardware.

This week OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled a custom chip built specifically to run large language models in production. Not for training. For inference — the moment a model actually serves a response to a user.

Why does this matter beyond the tech world? Because inference cost is the single biggest barrier between a promising AI prototype and a profitable AI product. Every API call, every chatbot response, every agent action costs money at the silicon level. Custom chips designed for this exact workload can fundamentally reshape those economics.

When the leading AI model company decides it needs its own silicon to serve its own models, it signals that the AI industry is entering a new phase. The competition is no longer just about who has the smartest model. It is about who can deploy intelligence most efficiently at global scale.

For business leaders, the question becomes: is your AI infrastructure positioned for the cost structures that are coming, or are you locked into economics that will be outpaced?
